analysis.investment_thesis: CP PLUS is India's leading CCTV/surveillance brand riding a genuine infrastructure tailwind, with 20% revenue CAGR — a classic Lynch "invest in what you know" story. But at P/E 105 with a PEG of ~4-5x and deeply suspicious earnings quality, the price kills the thesis entirely.
key_strengths: India's #1 surveillance brand — CP PLUS cameras visible in malls, banks, highways; consumer-observable market leadership
Revenue CAGR 20.2% and Operating Income CAGR 34.2% over 5 years — genuine margin expansion story
Ultra-low Debt/Equity of 0.08 and massive equity jump (INR 424 Cr → 1,587 Cr in 2025) — clean, well-capitalized balance sheet
key_risks: PEG ratio ~4-5x (P/E 105 ÷ ~20% sustainable growth) — Lynch's red line is 1.5; this is 3x above it
Catastrophic cash flow disconnect: INR 351 Cr net profit in FY25 vs only INR 27 Cr operating cash flow — earnings are not converting to cash
FY25 Other Income of INR 259 Cr (vs -12 Cr prior year) explains most of the profit jump — normalized earnings are ~180-200 Cr, implying true P/E closer to 130-150x
red_flags: Other Income of INR 259 Cr in FY25 is larger than the company's entire operating income (INR 248 Cr) — non-recurring and non-operational
Free Cash Flow was essentially zero (INR 1 Cr) in FY25 despite record reported profits — a hallmark of low earnings quality
Operating CF was -INR 180 Cr in FY24, only INR 27 Cr in FY25 — chronic working capital drag in a trading/distribution-heavy business model
analysis.detailed_analysis:
The business story is real — walk into any Indian shop, hospital, or highway toll booth and you'll see a CP PLUS camera. India's surveillance market is expanding rapidly driven by government smart-city projects, GST formalization of retail, and rising crime awareness. Revenue has compounded at 20% and operating margins have expanded from 4.6% to 11.2% over five years, which is exactly the kind of improving unit economics Lynch loves. The promoter holding of 76.91% signals conviction, and debt is negligible at 0.08x D/E.

But the valuation is indefensible for a Lynch-style GARP investor. The FY25 net profit of INR 351 Cr is a fiction — strip out the INR 259 Cr "Other Income" (likely a one-time asset sale or investment gain) and normalized earnings fall to roughly INR 150-180 Cr, implying a true P/E of 130-150x. Operating cash flow of just INR 27 Cr against INR 351 Cr reported profit is the loudest alarm bell possible. A PEG of 4-5x means you are paying four to five years of growth upfront. Lynch's rule: never pay more than 2x the growth rate in P/E. At P/E 105 vs 20% growth, this stock needs to triple its earnings just to reach a fair PEG of 1.0. The story is good; the price is a disaster.
